title: Daybreak KV probe notes (small experiments & todo)
content:
Context:
- Quick dawn session to validate a hypothesis from yesterday's p99 spike on small inputs (seq_len <= 64) when microbatching toggles between 4 and 8.
- Goal: reproduce a KV-cache miss/eviction pattern and collect minimal artifacts for SRE handoff if it recurs during peak.

Summary of hypothesis:
- When microbatch size grows from 4->8, some request paths bypass prefix-cache lookup due to race on cache insertion (race window ~5-10ms). This increases p99 by ~20-30ms. NVLink memory pressure + kernel preemption may amplify it.
- Possible contributors: KV shard imbalance, async insert ordering, hot-eviction when kv_kvset is near threshold.

Immediate checklist (today):
- [x] Re-run the small-input replay harness against canary cluster (canary-03) w/ microbatch=4 and 8 (captured traces).
- [x] Capture perf top + bpftrace on the exact interval where we see the 95->99 tail divergence.
- [ ] Run the targeted meminfo + nvlink counters during load to see if remote memory stalls spike.
- [ ] Create minimal reproducer harness (sequence length 32, 1K reqs, bursty arrival) and run with isolcpus pinned.

Repro commands (notes to self):
- Replayer: ./tools/replay_small_inputs --model f32-retain --seq 32 --requests 1000 --microbatch 8 --qps 400 --target canary-03
- Perf: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30  && sudo perf script | ./scripts/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
- bpftrace snippet (hot-paths): sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_ioctl /comm=="runtime-exec"/ { @[comm] = count(); }' -c './tools/replay_small_inputs ...'
- NVLink counters: nvidia-smi nvlink --query -l 1 --format=csv

Quick results from today's run (canary-03, microbatch switch):
- microbatch=4: p50=9ms p95=24ms p99=48ms
- microbatch=8: p50=11ms p95=28ms p99=76ms (sporadic spikes to 120ms observed at t=00:13:40)
- perf flame: top frames show 1) kv_store_insert 2) memmove 3) cudaMemcpyAsync (interleaved) 4) schedule (kernel preemption stacks)
- bpftrace shows a handful of ioctl/syscall spikes aligning with the p99 spike window.

Hypotheses and quick triage notes:
- There is a small window where cache insert hasn't committed to the shared prefix table, other workers continue without the cached prefix and perform full KV write -> increases CPU + NVLink activity.
- Kernel preemption (sometime schedule() shows up in traceback) suggests heavy CPU contention on the device-side worker threads. Pinning threads to isolated cores reduced p99 in a very small local run.

Immediate mitigations to test (order):
1) Increase kv_commit_timeout from 5ms -> 12ms for the canary to see if fewer misses reduce p99 (cheap config).
2) Force stronger KV lock granularity (experimentally widen bucket locks) for a short canary window. Might hurt throughput.
3) Autoscale policy change: allow one extra dedicated worker when seq_len <= 64 and microbatch >= 8 (trade cost for latency).

Longer term ideas:
- Add an internal fast-path: if insertion is in-flight, readers can wait for a microspin (<= 2ms) and then fallback to full compute. This reduces redundant compute but might add jitter for some requests.
- Rework KV insertion ordering to make commit idempotent and visible across workers in guaranteed order (requires careful testing with current raft-ish metadata).
- Add metric: kv_inflight_inserts per-shard and alert when > 10% of requests observe miss while inflight > X.

Notes for handoff to SRE / ticket content (short):
- Observed p99 spike on canary-03 during microbatch=8 runs. Attached: perf fold, bpftrace logs, nvlink counters, replayer args. Suspect race on kv insert + thread preemption. Suggested mitigations: bump kv_commit_timeout and pin device worker threads to cores; follow up with insertion reordering.

Open questions:
- Is there any recent change to the prefix hash function that could increase collisions? (check PRs merged last 2 weeks) -- TODO: grep commits between 2025-01-28..2025-02-10 for 'prefix_hash' or 'kv-bucket'.
- Could the CUDA driver update on canary-03 be contributing? nvlink firmware version shows a minor update on 2025-02-01. Check host image diffs.

Follow-ups (next 48h):
- Run canary with kv_commit_timeout=12ms and microbatch=8 for 6h window (owner: Matilda).
- Add a brief metric emitter for kv_inflight_inserts (owner: Hector).
- Try isolated-core pinning in staging with a few model replicas (owner: Ivy).
- Draft a short postmortem if this recurs during next peak (owner: Matilda).

Misc quick notes (random):
- Saw a strange log: "kv-shard-7: insert returned EEXIST but insertion_count++" -> possible race with double-insert path. Save grep: git grep -n "insert returned EEXIST" -- $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
- If we add the spin-wait fast-path, ensure we guard against thundering herd by exponential backoff.

End of morning session. Leaving collected artifacts in /tmp/matilda/daybreak-20250215/ (perf.folded, bpftrace.log, nvlink.csv, replay.args). Will sync to Jira ticket JIRA-RT-4021 after the first mitigation run.

(Notes to self) Reminders:
- Keep experiment durations short (<6h) to not skew cost.
- Notify #runtime-triage before the kv_commit_timeout bump.
